definitions.explanation: An extremely brief moment in time. Originally a Buddhist term for the shortest possible unit of time. Used in literary and dramatic contexts to describe a fleeting instant, often at a critical or climactic point.

examples.japanese: その{刹那|せつな}、{稲妻|いなずま}が{走|はし}った。
examples.english: At that very instant, lightning flashed.

examples.japanese: {目|め}が{合|あ}った{刹那|せつな}、{心臓|しんぞう}が{高鳴|たかな}った。
examples.english: The moment our eyes met, my heart began to race.

examples.japanese: {爆発|ばくはつ}の{刹那|せつな}、{彼|かれ}は{地面|じめん}に{伏|ふ}せて{難|なん}を{逃|のが}れた。
examples.english: At the instant of the explosion, he threw himself to the ground and escaped harm.

notes:
USAGE:
{刹那|せつな} is literary and dramatic. It typically appears in the pattern その{刹那|せつな} (at that very instant) or ～の{刹那|せつな} (at the moment of ~). Not used in everyday casual conversation — {瞬間|しゅんかん} is the neutral equivalent.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- その{刹那|せつな} (at that very instant)
- ～した{刹那|せつな} (the moment ~ happened)
- {一|いっ}{瞬|しゅん}の{刹那|せつな} (a fleeting instant)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{瞬間|しゅんかん} (moment/instant) is the standard, neutral word for a brief moment. {刹那|せつな} is more literary and carries a sense of dramatic tension. {刹那|せつな}{的|てき} (momentary, living for the moment) is a common derivative.
